children: Defense stocks have been in a bear market. You wouldn't know that from the earnings.

Thursday morning, L3Harris Technologies announced third-quarter earnings per share of $3.28, up 33% year over year, from sales of $6.1 billion, up 9% year over year on a comparable basis. Wall Street was looking for EPS of $2.99 from sales of $5.9 billion.

Guidance was nudged higher. Management now projects 2026 sales of about $23.6 billion, up from prior guidance of $23.5 billion. Unadjusted earnings per share are expected to be about $12.30, up from prior guidance of $11.90. Wall Street currently projects EPS of about $12.
Numbers look solid. L3Harris stock was up 6.5% in midday trading at $277.65, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 0.3% and 0.2%, respectively.

Shipbuilder Huntington Ingalls Industries also got in on the action. Shares were up 10.7% at $309.29 after the company reported earnings per share of $5.48. Wall Street was looking for $4.36. Management raised sales guidance to a midpoint of $10.6 billion, up from a prior midpoint of $10.3 billion.

The moves add to recent gains. L3Harris stock was at its 52-week low of $232.35 only days ago. Huntington stock was in the same situation. Its 52-week low was $255.36. Defense stocks have been mired in a long slump since the Iran war began, with investors worried that military spending could slow if Democrats retake Congress in the midterms.
Coming into Thursday's trading, L3Harris stock was down 29% since the start of the war. Huntington shares were off 30%.

Things started to turn around recently thanks to earnings. Lockheed Martin stock jumped 7% after it reported better-than-expected third-quarter numbers on Oct. 22. Northrop Grumman stock jumped 4.6% after reporting better-than-expected earnings on Oct. 20.
This was also the first quarter for new L3Harris CEO Sam Mehta. He replaced former CEO Christopher Kubasik in August after Kubasik stepped down following a board investigation into his conduct.
